function: ISAC transmit beamforming: ISACBeam-GNN outputs beamformers for several users and one 3D extended target, minimizing sensing CRB under SINR constraints or a weighted CRB and sum-rate objective (p. 6-7).
system: Monostatic MIMO ISAC: BS with 8x8 UPA, four single-antenna users, one 3D extended target; 30 GHz carrier, 1 GHz bandwidth; no RIS (p. 3, 8).
method: Graph neural network (sensing, communication, integration modules) trained unsupervised with a penalty-based loss using Adam, one network per problem P1 and P2 (p. 6-8).
data_channel: Own simulation only: Saleh-Valenzuela BS-user channel with 100 dB path loss, line-of-sight sensing; 10240 training, 2048 validation, 2048 test samples from random user and target locations (p. 8).
test_conditions: Trained with 4 users, 38 scatterers, SINR threshold 0 dB; tested with other numbers of users and scatterers without retraining. Same simulator for training and testing (p. 8, 11).
baselines: Non-learned only: Center Design, Average Design [21], and the SDR and SCA optimization solutions; no earlier learned beamformer is compared (p. 9-10).
metrics: Trace of CRB of kinematic parameters, SINR, sum rate, C&S trade-off curves, beampatterns, SINR-constraint satisfaction probability, average computation time (p. 9-11).
complexity: GNN inference O(max{KL, NtNcL, Nt^2 Nc}) flops; average time 0.71 s versus 49.78 s (CRB-min) and 125.42 s (WIM) for optimization (p. 8).
q1_support: p. 8: "We utilize the Saleh-Valenzuela channel model for the BS-CU link with a path loss of 100 dB." Custom simulator; no 3GPP, QuaDRiGa, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is named anywhere in the paper.
q2_support: p. 11: "The fixed ISACBeam-GNN is trained under Γ = 0 dB, Nc = 4 and K = 38 for P1 and P2" and then tested with other numbers of CUs and scatterers (Fig. 9a-c) without retraining.
q3_support: p. 9: "Two baselines are selected for comparison with our proposed beamforming designs", both optimization-based (Center Design, Average Design). No earlier learned beamformer is compared; the non-fixed GNN of Fig. 9 (p. 11) is a variant of the proposed method.
q4_support: p. 8: "ISACBeam-GNN achieves a significant reduction in flops and running time, as presented in Table I"; the paper gives O(2368K + 15360KL + 10496) for the sensing module and the overall order, and seconds in Table I.
q5_support: p. 8: "samples, which are randomly generated based on different CU and ET locations": data are self-generated. No code or data link, no public dataset and no measured data is stated anywhere in the paper.
notes: Preprint arXiv:2412.06353v2, titled '3D Extended Target Sensing in ISAC: Cramer-Rao Bound Analysis and Beamforming Design'; the DOI cannot be checked against the title from the PDF alone. Main contributions are the CRB analysis and two optimization-based beamformers (SDR, SCA; p. 5-6); the learned ISACBeam-GNN (p. 6-8) is the third contribution and is evaluated in Section VI-D (Table I, Figs. 7-9), so no_learning does not apply, but the learned part is secondary in the paper. Beamforming in an ISAC system is area 5. RIS appears only in related work (p. 2), not in the system, so ris is 0.
